title: Planner: AI-generated status reports in Planner Agent
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout, licensing and administrative controls are supported by the supplied Microsoft notice and Microsoft Learn. It correctly distinguishes the general agent controls from the Planner-specific PowerShell setting and preserves the unresolved difference between Microsoft's descriptions of report storage.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Exporting report content to a Copilot Page creates separately shareable content rather than confining it to the plan's membership.
claims.quote: Page Sharing: Grants access to a specific page (not the whole notebook) with options for edit or read-only access. The user can choose to use a company share link or people-specific share link, based on your organizational sharing settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified a separate report-creation identity for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Planner" "status reports" "identity"; Planner Agent status reports identity generation audit event disable reports separately. Read MC1506735 and Planner Agent access and Loop dependency pages; no separate report-creation identity specified.

claims.claim: The supplied notice describes user-requested drafting and refinement, not autonomous sending.
claims.quote: When an authorized user requests a report, Planner Agent uses information from a plan they can access to create a status report. ... It adds the ability to generate and refine a status report through Planner Agent chat using accessible plan information.

claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowPlannerCopilot $true -PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId <security group id> enables Planner Agent in Planner for a security group.
claims.quote: To turn on Planner Agent and Planner Agent chat for a specific security group: ... Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowPlannerCopilot $true -PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId <security group id>

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for the Planner-specific all-users or security-group setting represented by AllowPlannerCopilot and PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Agent AllowPlannerCopilot PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId admin UI security group restrict access status reports. Read learn.microsoft.com/planner/turn-off-planner-agent; it supplies PowerShell, not a UI for this setting.

claims.claim: The Planner-specific access instructions cover task execution and status reporting in Planner.
claims.quote: instructions for how to restrict access to the Planner Agent experience for task execution and status reporting in both basic and premium plans

claims.claim: The sources do not explicitly confirm that the Planner-specific PowerShell setting governs the new AI-generated reports in Planner Agent in Copilot.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Agent AllowPlannerCopilot PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId admin UI security group restrict access status reports. Read MC1506735 and turn-off-planner-agent; the latter directs Copilot agent management elsewhere, without mapping this feature to the cmdlet.

claims.claim: Planner-specific policy changes can take up to one hour.
claims.quote: Changes may take up to 1 hour to reflect across your organization.

claims.claim: The Planner access page directs administrators to Microsoft 365 admin center agent management for Planner Agent in Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: For information on how to manage the Planner Agent in Microsoft Copilot, please see Manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Disabling Loop also affects other Planner and Loop experiences, so it is not a report-specific control.
claims.quote: When Loop is disabled, users cannot create Loop task lists, so no tasks sync into Planner from them. ... When Loop is disabled, tasks from these meeting notes do not sync into Planner.
